title: Optimized electroporation of CRISPR-Cas9/gRNA ribonucleoprotein complex in human pluripotent stem cells
author: Xu, Kita, et al.
materials: Wizard® SV Gel and PCR Clean-Up System

steps.title: Coat plates and seed iPSCs
steps.instruction: Prepare feeder‑free, xeno‑free human iPSC cultures on iMatrix‑511 coated plates and grow to semi‑confluence (6–8 days).

substeps.instruction: Plate coating: Add 50 µL (30–60 µL) of iMatrix‑511 to 12 mL PBS, mix, and dispense 2 mL per well of a 6‑well plate (final 0.25–0.5 µg/cm²). For other plates use 1 mL for 12‑well, 500 µL for 24‑well, 100 µL for 96‑well. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 1–18 h (overnight gives tighter adhesion).
Aspirate coating buffer, add 2 mL StemFit AK02N (or AK03N) + 2 µL 10 mM Y‑27632 (final 10 µM) to each well and pre‑warm in the CO₂ incubator.

Passage iPSCs: aspirate media, wash 1–2 mL PBS, add 300 µL 0.5 × TrypLE Select, incubate 37 °C 10 min with gentle shaking every 3–4 min, add 1 mL StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632 and pipet to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Count cells and seed 1.0 × 10⁴–1.5 × 10⁴ cells into each iMatrix‑511‑coated 6‑well well containing 2 mL StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632. Incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Next day replace with 2 mL fresh StemFit; add Y‑27632 to a final 10 µM if many dead cells are observed. Change media every 2 days.
Allow colonies to grow to semi‑confluence (colonies < 2 mm, spaces between colonies) by day 6–8. Do not let cultures become over‑confluent.

steps.title: Design CRISPR gRNA target
steps.instruction: Plan the genome‑editing strategy, locate a suitable PAM, evaluate off‑targets, and prepare the DNA oligo for in‑vitro transcription.

substeps.instruction: Obtain the genomic region surrounding the desired edit (UCSC, NCBI, or IGV).
Search for an NGG (or CCN on the reverse strand) PAM within a 10–20 bp window of the target; the cut site is 3 bp upstream of the PAM.
Select several candidate gRNAs, check off‑target sites with CRISPRdirect or CRISPOR, preferring guides with few off‑targets (≤ 3 bp mismatch) and mismatches in the seed region (≤ 10 bp from PAM).

If the target sequence does not start with G or GG, add one or two G residues at the 5′ end of the guide for efficient T7 transcription, or order chemically synthesized gRNA that matches the exact target.

steps.title: Generate IVT gRNA template
steps.instruction: Create a DNA template for T7‑driven transcription by PCR amplification of the designed oligo.

substeps.instruction: Design a forward primer containing the T7 promoter and the 20‑nt guide (add GG or G as needed) and use the universal reverse primer (5′‑AAAGCACCGACTCGGTGCCACTTTTTCAAGTTGATAACGGACTAGCCTTATTTAACTTGCTATTTCTAGCTCTAAAAC‑3′).

Set up a 50 µL PCR with: 33 µL ultrapure H₂O, 5 µL 10 × buffer, 0.3 µL 2 mM dNTPs, 1.5 µL 25 mM MgSO₄, 0.3 µL 10 µM T7‑fwd primer, 0.3 µL 10 µM T7‑rev primer, 1 µL KOD‑Plus‑Neo (1 U/µL), 1 µL template DNA.
Cycling: 98 °C 30 s; 30 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 50 °C 30 s, 68 °C 15 s; final extension 72 °C 10 min; hold at 4 °C.
Run the product on a 2 % agarose gel, excise the 121–123 bp band, extract DNA, elute in 20–30 µL RNase‑free water.
Measure DNA concentration (aim for ≥ 20 ng/µL, preferably 20–50 ng/µL).

steps.title: In‑vitro transcribe gRNA
steps.instruction: Synthesize gRNA using the MEGAshortscript™ T7 kit and purify to a concentration ≥ 1 µg/µL.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 20 µL transcription mix: 2 µL 10 × reaction buffer, 2 µL 75 mM GTP, 2 µL 75 mM ATP, 2 µL 75 mM CTP, 2 µL 75 mM UTP, 2 µL T7 Enzyme Mix, ≤ 4 µL template DNA (75–150 ng), add water to 20 µL.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight (12–18 h).
Add 1 µL TURBO DNase, incubate 37 °C 15 min to remove template DNA.
Purify RNA with the RNeasy MinElute Cleanup Kit; elute in 30–40 µL RNase‑free water to obtain ≥ 1 000 ng/µL gRNA.
Aliquot 5–10 µL (5–10 µg) per tube, store at –80 °C; minimize freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Design and reconstitute ssODN
steps.instruction: Prepare a single‑stranded oligodeoxynucleotide donor for HDR.

substeps.instruction: For single‑base edits, place the desired nucleotide in the centre of the ssODN and add 30–60 nt (typically 50 nt) homology arms on each side; locate the edit 5′ of the Cas9 cut site. Include a silent mutation at the PAM (or seed region) to prevent recutting.
For loxP knock‑in, use the 34 bp loxP sequence (ATAACTTCGTATAGCATACATTATACGAAGTTAT) and optionally add “TC” to create an XmnI site for screening.
Order the ssODN (freeze‑dried) from a supplier (e.g., Fasmac, IDT, Hokkaido System Science) with basic reverse‑phase purification (HPLC if higher efficiency is needed).
Dissolve the ssODN in ultrapure water to 10 µg/µL (high concentration is critical). Note: use water rather than TE buffer for MaxCyte electroporation; TE buffer is acceptable for 4D‑Nucleofector.

steps.title: Prepare iPSC subcloning plates
steps.instruction: Harvest semi‑confluent iPSCs and coat 96‑well plates for single‑cell cloning.

substeps.instruction: Dissociate cells with 0.5 × TrypLE Select as described in the iPSC preparation section.
Coat three 96‑well plates with iMatrix‑511 (add 2 mL of iMatrix solution per well as in step 1) at least 1–24 h before seeding.
If a cell sorter is available, proceed to step 7 (single‑cell sorting); otherwise continue with step 8 (limit dilution).

steps.title: Single‑cell sort into 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Isolate individual iPSCs by fluorescence‑activated cell sorting.

substeps.instruction: Perform the dissociation steps from step 1 (sections b–d).
Count live cells with a hemocytometer and trypan blue.
Transfer 1.0–10.0 × 10⁵ live cells into a 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge 120 × g 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 300 µL FACS buffer (2 % FBS in PBS) and filter through a 5 mL flow tube with a cell strainer.
Sort 1 cell per well into the pre‑coated 96‑well plate using a BD FACS Aria II (or equivalent).
Incubate the sorted plate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Limit‑dilution subcloning (optional)
steps.instruction: Generate single‑cell derived colonies by serial dilution.

substeps.instruction: Dissociate cells as in step 1 (sections b–d).
Count live cells, transfer 1.0 × 10⁴ cells into a 15 mL tube containing 10 mL StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632.

Create three dilutions: add 10 µL, 30 µL, and 100 µL of the cell suspension into separate 15 mL tubes each containing 10 mL StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632, yielding ~10, 30, and 100 cells per 10 mL respectively.
Remove the iMatrix coating buffer from the 96‑well plates prepared in step 6.
Add 100 µL of each diluted suspension to individual wells (use a multichannel pipette, keep the suspension mixed).
Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Next day, examine wells under a microscope; retain wells that contain a single cell and discard wells with >1 cell.

steps.title: Culture subclones and expand
steps.instruction: Maintain single‑cell derived colonies, passage, and prepare for genotyping.

substeps.instruction: Every 2–3 days add 50 µL fresh StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632 to each well (do not completely remove existing media).
On day 6–7 replace media with StemFit without Y‑27632.
Monitor colonies; visible colonies appear day 7–10. Discard wells with >2 colonies, keep wells with a single colony.
Continue adding 50 µL fresh StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632 every 2 days.
When a colony reaches 100–300 µm (≈ day 9–11), transfer the entire well to a well of a 24‑well plate containing StemFit + Y‑27632.
Change media in the 24‑well plates every 2 days until cultures become semi‑confluent.

steps.title: Extract DNA and genotype clones
steps.instruction: Isolate genomic DNA from each subclone, freeze‑store cells, and screen for the intended edit.

substeps.instruction: When subclones are semi‑confluent, split the culture: extract genomic DNA from half of the cells using the MonoFas gDNA Cultured Cells Extraction Kit (or similar) and elute in 40 µL buffer.
Freeze‑store the remaining half of the cells in STEM‑CELLBANKER as a backup stock.
Perform PCR amplification of the target locus for each clone and submit the products for Sanger sequencing (or restriction‑enzyme screening if a diagnostic site was introduced).

Identify clones carrying the desired knockout or knock‑in; retain at least three positive clones for downstream validation (protein expression, phenotype, pluripotency, differentiation, genomic integrity).

description: The discovery of CRISPR-Cas9 has made tremendous progress in various research areas especially for genetic functions, disease modeling, and gene therapy (Dastidar et al., 2018; Ran et al., 2013; Soldner and Jaenisch, 2018; Zhong et al., 2020). This technology is widely applied to human PSCs, which have a great potential for regenerative medicine and cell therapies. With this in mind, the protocol utilizes feeder-free, xeno-free human PSCs cultured on recombinant Laminin-511 (iMatrix-511) with StemFit AK02N (or AK03N) media. For successful genome editing, the method to introduce Cas9/gRNA complex into cells is critical. Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) form of delivery has several advantages over the DNA/RNA form (Gee et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2014; Paquet et al., 2016; Richardson et al., 2016; Zuris et al., 2015), since the RNP functions immediately, degrades quickly, and is relatively smaller than plasmid DNA or mRNA. Furthermore, the pre-formed Cas9/gRNA RNP complex can evade the inhibition by cellular mRNA (Kagita et al., 2021). In addition to Cas9/gRNA, single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotides (ssODNs) must be available at the DNA repair site as a template for homology directed repair (HDR) pathway. In this protocol, we introduce Cas9/gRNA RNP complex and ssODN together into human PSCs by utilizing MaxCyte or 4D-Nucleofector electroporators, which were superior for inducing HDR. Also, this protocol can be applied for single nucleotide editing for disease modeling and correcting mutations in PSCs, since more than half of disease-associated genetic changes are single nucleotide polymorphisms (Bamshad et al., 2011; Collins et al., 1997). Moreover, a 34 bp loxP sequence can be inserted for further genomic engineering by Cre recombination (Branda and Dymecki, 2004; Sauer and Henderson, 1988). Additionally, by simply omitting an ssODN, a small (∼10 nt) indel may be introduced for knocking out a target gene.
